title: [sweep] Two user-visible labels the authoring contract cannot express a translation for (#5377 #5728)
body:
Sweep card (maintainer-directed, 2026-08-07). One claim, one PR, two `Fixes`.

## Admission criterion

> A **user-visible label** that the platform otherwise translates, which the **authoring contract cannot express a translation for** — the author has no legal way to write the localized value.

| # | Surface | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| **#5377** | view tab labels (`tabs[].label`) | no translation key and no resolver — the list-page tab bar is untranslatable in every locale |
| **#5728** | `component.zod.ts`'s `I18nLabelSchema` key | declared as a plain string, while **3 platform pages author inline multilingual maps at 31 sites** — i.e. real authoring already exceeds the declaration |

Both are authoring-surface gaps, and both are `target:v17`. #5728 is the sharper one: the declaration is already contradicted by in-repo authored metadata, so either the sites are wrong or the schema is.

## Explicitly NOT members (same topic, different review face)

- **#5199** (`report` / `dataset` have no translator at all) — that is **runtime translator wiring**, not an authoring-surface widening. Different mechanism, different reviewer question; it stays its own card.
- **#4426** (flow / workflow authorable label + node translation contract) — currently `pm:on-hold`; a held card may not ride a sweep.

Recording the exclusions because "i18n" is a *topic*, not an admission criterion — bundling by topic is exactly what the same-class rule forbids.

## Direction (state per member)

Each member widens the authoring surface (add the key + resolver / accept the inline map form) **or** rules the current authoring wrong and corrects the 31 sites. #5728 cannot be settled without deciding which side is authoritative — say which, with the site count as evidence.

## Scope discipline

- **Zero changes beyond the two members**; `git diff --stat` corresponds to the checklist.
- A widened schema may not shrink the refusal surface: shapes that are genuinely invalid keep rejecting, verbatim.
- Out-of-scope findings filed separately per PD #10.

## Landing constraints

Touches `packages/spec` generated baselines ⇒ os-regen four-step序; `check:authorable-surface` green; ⛔ never hand-edit the anchor. If the ruling lands on "correct the 31 sites", the platform-page edits ride the same PR and appear in the checklist.

## Review shape

By checklist: one line per member — surface | what an author can write today | what they can write after | which side was ruled authoritative.

Filed unassigned. Member issues keep `pm:queue` but are **excluded from batch selection while this card is open**; both close with the PR.
